title: Where to Watch the 100th Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade for Free to See Queen Latifah, LL Cool J & Dolly Parton Tribute
summary: The centennial event will take place Saturday, Nov. 28, at 8:30 a.m. ET on NBC and Telemundo, but you can watch across several streaming platforms with a free trial.
contentText:

This year’s Macy’s Thanksgiving Day Parade is marking a few milestones: Its 100th anniversary and the first time in history that it’s ever been postponed.

Originally scheduled for Thanksgiving Day (Nov. 26), the parade was postponed to Saturday (Nov. 28) due to disruptions from strong winds and potential flooding across New York. Safety concerns surrounding the giant balloons also put their participation in question. The parade is scheduled to air live at 8:30 a.m. ET on NBC and Telemundo and stream on Peacock , though viewers should keep an eye out for weather-related updates.

Parade officials say that 95% of the originally scheduled acts will perform on Saturday. However, the Macy’s Great American Marching Band and the University of Alabama’s Million Dollar Band will be unable to participate due to scheduling conflicts. The lineup will also feature surprise additions from LL Cool J and Gloria Gaynor.

This year’s celebration is going big with a record-breaking 100 inflatables, including new balloons featuring Bluey, Hello Kitty, Mickey Mouse and Underdog. Music fans are in for a treat , with RAYE opening the festivities , followed by scheduled performances from Megan Moroney, Teddy Swims, Queen Latifah, JoJo, RIIZE, EJAE, Keke Palmer, Anthony Ramos and Jimmy Fallon & The Roots. The lineup also includes a special Dolly Parton tribute by Megan Hilty and a Broadway showcase. Savannah Guthrie, Hoda Kotb and Al Roker return to host NBC’s coverage, bringing viewers along for all the parade-day excitement.

At a Glance: Where to Watch the 100th Macy’s Day Parade for Free Online

- Date & Time: Saturday, Nov. 28, 2026, at 8:30 a.m. ET

- TV Channel: NBC & Telemundo (Spanish-language broadcast)

- Stream: Peacock (no free trial), Prime Video , DirecTV , Fubo and Hulu + Live TV (free trials).
